key_insight: Autoregressive output length (number of response tokens) is a primary bottleneck for vision–language model latency; rethinking inference as a coordinated multi-agent process and adapting token budgets per model can unlock substantial efficiency gains.
problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch between model capability and token-generation cost: VLM latency is often dominated by sequential LLM decoding, and different models require very different output-token counts to reach comparable performance—creating an opportunity to optimize end-to-end inference.
method: Comprehensive latency breakdown across VLM components (vision encoder, prompt processing, LLM decoding) using simulated workloads to identify where time is spent.

Introduce a multi-agent inference perspective: distribute decoding responsibilities among specialized/parallel agents and apply adaptive token budgets or early-exit strategies to reduce unnecessary autoregressive steps.
Analyze token-count vs. performance trade-offs across models to guide when to apply agent coordination, token-limiting, or model selection for deployment.
impact: Provides practical guidance for reducing inference latency and cost when deploying VLMs by focusing optimization on output-token generation and using multi-agent/adaptive decoding strategies—helpful for engineers building real-time or resource-constrained applications.
visual_elements: Stacked bar chart: latency breakdown per component (vision encoder | prompt prep | LLM decoding) to show decoding dominance
Scatter plot: number of output tokens vs. task performance for multiple VLMs, highlighting variability and diminishing returns
System diagram: multi-agent inference architecture showing parallel/specialized agents, token budget controller, and early-exit paths
Flowchart: decision policy for adaptive token allocation (input complexity → agent selection → token limit → consolidate outputs)
paper_title: Rethinking Model Efficiency: Multi-Agent Inference with Large Models
paper_authors: Sixun Dong, Juhua Hu, Steven Li, Wei Wen, Qi Qian
